item.title: Democrat wants DHS to examine possible bias in Minneapolis investigations
item.description: Sen. Maggie Hassan asked the DHS inspector general to examine potential bias in Minneapolis shooting investigations.

item.title: Lawyers, lawsuit plaintiffs speak out about ICE
item.description: ACLU lawsuits accuse ICE of violating First and Fourth Amendment rights through intimidation, surveillance, and unlawful arrests in Minnesota.

item.title: Best at Work Insights: The choice we’re making about artificial intelligence
item.description: Experts say poor training and loss of connection undermine real workplace benefits of artificial intelligence.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump’s global tariffs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that President Trump exceeded his authority by imposing global tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

item.title: With AI, Supreme Court is seen as well as heard
item.description: A free AI-powered tool called On the Docket uses video to make U.S. Supreme Court rulings more accessible amid declining public trust.

item.title: Perspectives: Trump might be right on filibuster objection
item.description: An analysis of the Senate filibuster’s constitutional flaws, political impacts, and legal challenges amid shutdowns, elections disputes, and DHS funding battles.

item.title: With tariffs ruling, Supreme Court reasserts its power to check Trump​
item.description: The court reasserts its role as a check on the other branches of government including the president, after a year when legal scholars had increasingly voiced doubts.

item.title: Three recommended for 3rd District judgeship
item.description: The Commission on Judicial Selection recommends John Brooks, Holli Mayer, and Sarah Palm for the 3rd Judicial District judgeship in Minnesota.

item.title: Judge orders secrecy for report on Trump classified-documents case
item.description: A Florida federal judge blocked the public release of special counsel Jack Smith's report on Trump's classified documents case, citing grand jury secrecy and presumption of innocence.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court to hear bid by oil companies to toss climate suits
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear ExxonMobil and Suncor's appeal to dismiss a Boulder, Colorado, climate change lawsuit seeking damages for fossil fuel impacts.
